clue.text: Cover for cut cake

definitions.meaning: a sticking dressing put over a small wound
as a verb, to coat thickly, as mud cakes boots

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a sticky dressing for a wound, and the verb for smearing a thick layer over something.

clue.text: Postman caught on Harley … extremely irregular

parts.note: Postman Pat is a British children's TV character
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A postman on a Harley-Davidson motorbike who rides very unpredictably.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is the title character of a British children's TV series about a village postman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uneven in quality, good in places and poor in others, is irregular.

clue.text: Take on one animal and return another

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: return says the second animal is read backwards

parts.note: another animal here is the emu, a big flightless bird

explanation.surface: Taking on one animal at the zoo and giving back a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a role or responsibility is to adopt it, as in to assume command.

clue.text: A glare from you once sat with horrid Yankee on vacation

parts.note: thee is an old form of you
vile means horrid

indicators.note: on vacation says the word is emptied out, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned way to describe a nasty American sitting beside you.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent stare said to cast a curse is a glare in the most hostile sense.

clue.text: Upbringing of some Saudi girls is strict

indicators.note: Upbringing says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The way some girls in Saudi Arabia are brought up is strict.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Upbringing' means bringing up, so the hidden letters are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbending and severe is strict, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Soft area in New Delhi for place to land

indicators.note: in says the soft-and-area pair sits inside the reworked city letters
New says the letters of Delhi are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Somewhere soft to touch down in the Indian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like part of the city's name, but it signals the anagram: DELHI becomes HELID, and 'in' places PA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is a marked landing spot for a helicopter, so it is literally a spot for touching down.

clue.text: Tricky problem of stolen vessel at bottom of Sargasso

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
a pot is a vessel

indicators.note: bottom of points to the final letter, the lowest in a down entry

explanation.surface: A stolen ship lying on the floor of the Sargasso Sea makes a tricky problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate issue nobody wants to handle is a tricky problem in idiom.

clue.text: Obscene wife in jail (she confessed finally)

indicators.note: in says the wife goes inside the collected final letters
finally takes the final letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A wife locked up for indecency who eventually owned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude and indecent is obscene, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Convince most of the country with broadcast material

indicators.note: most of says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Peru is the South American country

indicators.note: broadcast says the word is to be heard rather than seen

parts.note: suede is a soft leather material

explanation.surface: Win over most of a nation using broadcast material, like propaganda.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone is to win them round, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tragedy when upset fellow stood on flower

indicators.note: stood on in a down entry means it sits on top of the next piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid is a man's name, a fellow
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A calamity when an angry man trampled a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a tragedy, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Sensors locate son in gallery with American friends

indicators.note: locate son in gallery: the son is placed within the gallery's letters

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
bud, short for buddy, is US slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Instructions to find a boy somewhere in an art gallery alongside some American pals.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TATE is a London art gallery; S goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The small organs on the tongue detect flavour, so they are sensors in the literal sense.

clue.text: Approach understood by old departments

parts.note: to have got something is to have understood it
a hospital's wards are its departments

explanation.surface: An approach that the old departments of an organisation took on board.
explanation.definitionFit: To head in the direction of something is to draw near it, a verb-phrase synonym.

clue.text: Films setter in dodgy Soho dive

indicators.note: in says the setter goes inside the rearranged letters
dodgy suggests something unsound or shaken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter of the puzzle refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The crossword setter has been filmed in a seedy bar in London's Soho.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a London district known for nightlife; 'dodgy' scrambles SOHO DIVE to HOVIDEOS, with 'in' marking where the setter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Recordings people make on camcorders at home are films in the plural, matching the noun.

clue.text: See 9
The German tracks prisoner climbing heath and bog

indicators.note: tracks means follows behind, so the article comes after the prisoner

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war
der is the German for the

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means going upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a moor is open heath

explanation.surface: A German follows a fugitive across heath and boggy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bog' looks like marshland next to heath, but it is British slang for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' lavatory, in genteel speech, is a toilet, which is a bog in British slang.

clue.text: Cross City supporter is against draw

indicators.note: against means up next to, so the drawing word sits right beside the others

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the city
a bra is an undergarment that supports
to doodle is to draw idly

explanation.surface: A football fan of a club called City is opposed to a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City supporter' reads as a football fan, but it is LA and BRA; 'draw' looks like a tied match but means sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: This dog is a crossbreed of a Labrador and a poodle, so it is literally a cross.

clue.text: Perhaps glossy bag under counter is something attractive?

indicators.note: under in a down entry means coming below, so these pieces follow the counter

parts.note: a bar is a counter in a pub
a glossy is a magazine, a mag
to net is to catch, or bag

explanation.surface: A glossy handbag tucked under a shop counter might be eye-catching.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight magnet literally attracts iron, so it is something attractive in the physical sense.

clue.text: One medic fixing broken hip starts to inspire awe in a class

parts.note: A means one

indicators.note: fixing says the doctor's letters hold the reworked letters in place

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

indicators.note: broken says the letters are rearranged
starts to takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A doctor mending a broken hip in an impressive way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges HIP to PHI; 'fixing' has the medic hold those letters, and 'in a class' sets up the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogs, newts and their kin form a taxonomic grouping of vertebrates, a class.

clue.text: Asked to strip and reveal frame

indicators.note: to strip means to peel off the outer layer, so the outside letters go

parts.note: to let on is to reveal

explanation.surface: Someone asked to undress and show their body.
explanation.definitionFit: The bones of a body form its supporting frame.

clue.text: Old Impressionist and I may do work to order around Spain

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the country code
to order means arranged as required, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A painter of the Impressionist school offering to work to commission.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Yarwood was a famous British TV impersonator of the 1970s; 'Impressionist' suggests Monet.
explanation.definitionFit: He made his name doing impressions of politicians, so he is an impressionist of a past era.

clue.text: Organised drug to be taken on Oscar's last day of freedom?

indicators.note: on in a down entry means placed after
to be taken says the drug is removed from the word

parts.note: staged means organised, as in staged an event
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Organised drug-taking at Oscar's party.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag do is a British bachelor party, the groom's last night as a single man.
explanation.definitionFit: A party before a wedding is playfully the groom's last day of freedom.

clue.text: Put down swan with Edward in attendance

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
Ned is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A swan being put down with Edward present.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing words is putting them down on paper, past tense.

clue.text: A portion of veal possibly hot rather than cold

indicators.note: rather than says one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: veal is the meat of a young calf, so it suggests the animal
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A serving of veal, preferably hot rather than cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot and cold read as serving temperatures but are the tap letters H and C.
explanation.definitionFit: One of two equal parts is a portion of a whole.

clue.text: Mangle turned in former cleaning outfit

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the word for former

parts.note: late can mean former, as in the late president

indicators.note: to mangle is to mess up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned mangle, the wringer once used to squeeze wet washing, being turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mangle' looks like the laundry wringer; it signals an anagram of TURNED, giving UNDRET.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service laundry is a business, an outfit where clothes are washed.

clue.text: Nick criminal clambering over top of the hospital

indicators.note: over says the reversed letters arch around the next piece
clambering in a down entry means climbing upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter

explanation.surface: A criminal climbs over the hospital roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like slang for arrest; it means a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cut or indentation is a nick.

clue.text: Sailors banned from core part of ship

indicators.note: banned from says the sailors are removed from the word

parts.note: a kernel is a core
RN, Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors barred from the heart of the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The spine running along the bottom of a hull is a structural part of a ship.

clue.text: Total fanatic is after British species of tree

indicators.note: is after says the following pieces come behind the abbreviation

parts.note: utter means total, as in utter nonsense
a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A complete obsessive is pursuing something British.
explanation.definitionFit: The white walnut of North America is a kind of tree, so it names one species.

clue.text: See 28
Ring lady needing university permit

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A woman needs a university's permission to get a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture and heraldry this is a small band or circle, a ring.

clue.text: Actor with car collecting working daughter's instrument

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer

indicators.note: collecting says the car takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: Morgan is a British sports car maker
on means working, as in the machine is on
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An actor with a car picks up his working daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Morgan is a British sports car brand.
explanation.definitionFit: This electric keyboard is a musical instrument familiar from jazz and rock.
